newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh PM wants to raise budget gap to 3.5 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh PM wants to raise budget gap to 3.5 pct/GDP.

text.p: Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Thursday the oil-rich republic's 1997 budget deficit could be increased to 3.5 percent of gross domestic product from the planned 3.16 percent.
However Kazhelgeldin told reporters he would keep the budget deficit within what he called European norms.
"We would not like to drop European standards (for the budget deficit)," he said.
He said the increased deficit would be financed through new debt issues, both at home and abroad. Kazhegeldin said he would like to see new government debt issued over longer terms.
The prime minister, speaking during a meeting with officials of Deutsche Bank AG said he would bring the issue before the Kazakh parliament. He gave no further details.

A cloud hangs over the reformist prime minister after Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev threatened to sack him if he failed to redress the former Soviet republic's backlog of unpaid wages and pensions.

Nazarbayev has given Kazhegeldin an April 10 deadline to come up with a plan to battle the payments crisis. Rumours of Kazhegeldin's imminent departure from government have been circulating for weeks, although on Wednesday he played down the sacking threat.
Kazakhstan's longest term paper is a dollar-denominated three-year Eurobond. The $200 million issue was snapped up by western investors in December.
The existing government budget for 1997 provides for 40.6 billion tenge in external borrowing, with internal borrowing set at 14.3 billion tenge.
In November, international rating agencies Moody's and Standard & Poor"s gave Kazakhstan Ba3 and BB- ratings respectively for its long-term foreign currency debt.
